member.name: M:Syncfusion.Telemetry.HttpTelemetrySender.SendAsync(Syncfusion.Telemetry.TelemetryBatch,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Sends a batch of telemetry events to Application Insights asynchronously.
Flow: 1. Send to Syncfusion endpoint (primary, synchronous) 2. Check if CustomerInsightsManager is configured (static variable) 3. If configured and valid: Send same telemetry to customer endpoint (async, fire-and-forget)
member.param: The telemetry batch containing events to send.
A cancellation token to cancel the operation.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous operation.
member.remarks:
All exceptions are silently caught to ensure telemetry failures never impact the application. Uses a fast timeout to quickly detect network unavailability without blocking. Cross-platform compatible with Blazor, MAUI, WinUI, .NET Core, etc.
AUTOMATIC DUAL-LOGGING: If CustomerInsightsManager.IsConfigured is true, telemetry is automatically sent to both Syncfusion and customer endpoints without any additional code.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Telemetry.HttpTelemetrySender.EnsureAwsLogStreamExistsAsync(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary:
Creates the AWS CloudWatch Logs log stream if it doesn't already exist. CRITICAL: This must be called before PutLogEvents API.
AWS CloudWatch requires the log stream to exist before you can write log events to it. This method calls the CreateLogStream API, which: - Returns HTTP 200 on success (first time) - Returns HTTP 409 on subsequent calls (stream already exists - ignored) - Returns HTTP 404 if log group doesn't exist (rare - customer should create manually)

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Telemetry.Telemetry.EnableCustomerInsights(Syncfusion.Telemetry.TelemetryOptions)
member.summary: Enables customer Azure Insights logging with the specified connection string.
member.param: The telemetry options containing customer connection details.
member.returns: A indicating success or failure.
member.remarks:
This method validates the customer's connection string through three layers: Layer 1: Format validation (Base64 decoding, structure) Layer 2: Semantic validation (GUID format, HTTPS URL) Layer 3: Connectivity validation (HTTP test to endpoint)
If validation succeeds, all future telemetry will be sent to both Syncfusion and customer Azure Insights. If validation fails, telemetry continues to be sent only to Syncfusion.
This method never throws an exception. All errors are captured in the result.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Telemetry.CustomerInsightsManager.SetupCustomerInsights(System.String)
member.summary:
Sets up customer Azure Application Insights with validation.
This method should be called once during application startup (in Main() or Program.cs). It validates the connection string through all 3 layers (syntax, semantic, connectivity) and stores the validated configuration for use throughout the application.
After successful setup, all telemetry events are automatically logged to both Syncfusion and customer endpoints.
member.param: The Base64-encoded Azure Application Insights connection string.
member.returns:
A CustomerInsightsValidationResult indicating success or failure.
If successful (IsValid = true): - Customer insights is configured and ready - All telemetry will be logged to both endpoints - IngestionEndpoint will be set
If failed (IsValid = false): - Check Message property for error details - Telemetry will continue with Syncfusion endpoint only - Customer insights will not be used
member.remarks:
Thread-safe. Can be called from multiple threads, but typically called once during application startup.
This method never throws exceptions. All validation errors are captured in the returned result object.
VALIDATION LAYERS: - Layer 1 (Syntax): Validates Base64 encoding and key-value structure - Layer 2 (Semantic): Validates GUID format and HTTPS URL - Layer 3 (Connectivity): Tests HTTP connectivity to the endpoint
If any layer fails, the configuration is not stored and an error is returned.

member.summary:
Sets up AWS CloudWatch Logs with validation.
This method should be called once during application startup (in Program.cs or Main()). It validates the connection string through all 3 layers (syntax, semantic, connectivity) and stores the validated configuration for use throughout the application.
After successful setup, all telemetry events are automatically logged to both Syncfusion and AWS CloudWatch endpoints.
member.param: The Base64-encoded AWS connection string. Format: AccessKeyId=AKIA...;SecretAccessKey=wJal...;Region=us-east-1;LogGroupName=/my-app/telemetry;LogStreamName=stream1
member.returns:
A CustomerInsightsValidationResult indicating success or failure.
If successful (IsValid = true): - AWS CloudWatch is configured and ready - All telemetry will be logged to both endpoints - IngestionEndpoint will contain the AWS endpoint URL
If failed (IsValid = false): - Check Message property for error details - Telemetry will continue with Syncfusion endpoint only - AWS CloudWatch will not be used
member.remarks:
Thread-safe. Can be called from multiple threads, but typically called once during application startup.
This method never throws exceptions. All validation errors are captured in the returned result object.
VALIDATION LAYERS: - Layer 1 (Format): Validates Base64 encoding and key-value structure - Layer 2 (Semantic): Validates AWS key format and region code - Layer 3 (Connectivity): Tests AWS API connection to verify credentials
If any layer fails, the configuration is not stored and an error is returned.

The Base64-encoded connection string for the platform. Format depends on platform: - Azure: InstrumentationKey=...;IngestionEndpoint=... - AWS: AccessKeyId=...;SecretAccessKey=...;Region=...;LogGroupName=...
member.returns:

If successful (IsValid = true): - Platform is configured and ready - All telemetry will be logged to this platform - IngestionEndpoint will be set

member.summary:
Parses the AWS connection string.
Expected connection string format (Base64-encoded): AccessKeyId=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE;SecretAccessKey=wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY;Region=us-east-1;LogGroupName=/my-app/telemetry;LogStreamName=stream1

SECURITY NOTE: The connection string should be stored securely and never logged. The parsed AccessKeyId and SecretAccessKey are kept in memory.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Telemetry.AwsConnectionStringValidator
member.summary:
Validates AWS CloudWatch connection credentials through three layers.
LAYER 1: FORMAT VALIDATION - Access Key ID format (AKIA/ASIA + 16 chars) - Secret Access Key not empty - Region code valid format - Log Group Name valid characters (alphanumeric, -, _, /, .)
LAYER 2: SEMANTIC VALIDATION - Access Key ID matches AWS pattern - Secret Access Key is base64-decodable - Region is in known AWS regions list - Log Group Name is non-empty
LAYER 3: CONNECTIVITY VALIDATION - Call AWS DescribeLogStreams API - Verify credentials work with AWS - Verify Log Group exists - 10-second timeout
USAGE: ------ var validator = new AwsConnectionStringValidator(); var result = validator.Validate(accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, region, logGroupName, logStreamName); if (result.IsValid) Console.WriteLine("✓ AWS credentials are valid"); else Console.WriteLine($"✗ Validation failed: {result.Message}");

member.summary:
Generates AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) authorization headers.
AWS SigV4 is the standard authentication mechanism for all AWS APIs. This class handles the cryptographic signing required by CloudWatch Logs API.
PROCESS: 1. Create canonical request string from HTTP request 2. Create string to sign with timestamp and region 3. Calculate HMAC-SHA256 signature using AWS credentials 4. Format as Authorization header
USAGE: ------ var signer = new AwsSigV4Signer(accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, region, "logs"); var headers = signer.GetAuthHeaders(httpMethod, payload, timestamp); // Add headers to HTTP request
REFERENCE: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/signature-version-4.html
